# pigz - Parallel Implementation of GZip

pigz (pronounced "pig-zee") is a parallel implementation of gzip that compresses files using multiple processors and cores.

## What pigz does

pigz is a fully functional replacement for gzip that exploits multiple processors and multiple cores to compress data faster. It can compress and decompress files in gzip, zlib, and zip formats.

## Basic Usage

```
pigz [options] [files...]
unpigz [options] [files...]
```

If no files are specified or "-" is given as a filename, pigz reads from standard input.

## Key Features

- **Parallel compression**: Splits input into chunks (default 128 KB) and compresses them in parallel
- **Multiple output formats**: Supports gzip, zlib, and single-entry zip formats
- **Compatible with gzip**: Can decompress any gzip file; gzip can decompress any pigz-compressed file
- **Independent blocks**: Optional mode for partial error recovery and random access
- **rsyncable**: Optional mode for rsync-friendly output

## Common Options

- **-#** (1-9, 11): Set compression level (1=fastest, 9=best, 11=zopfli for maximum compression)
- **-d, --decompress**: Decompress files
- **-k, --keep**: Keep original files (don't delete after compression)
- **-c, --stdout**: Write output to stdout
- **-p n**: Use n processors (default: all available)
- **-b n**: Set block size to n KB (default: 128)
- **-i, --independent**: Compress blocks independently
- **-R, --rsyncable**: Make output rsync-friendly
- **-l, --list**: List contents of compressed files
- **-t, --test**: Test integrity of compressed files
- **-f, --force**: Force overwrite of output files
- **-r, --recursive**: Recursively compress directories
- **-z, --zlib**: Use zlib format instead of gzip
- **-K, --zip**: Use zip format (single entry)
- **-v, --verbose**: Verbose output
- **-h, --help**: Display help

## Examples

Compress a file using all available processors:
```
pigz file.txt
```

Compress with maximum compression (slower):
```
pigz -11 file.txt
```

Decompress a file:
```
pigz -d file.txt.gz
# or
unpigz file.txt.gz
```

Compress to stdout:
```
pigz -c file.txt > file.txt.gz
```

Compress with 4 processors and keep the original:
```
pigz -k -p 4 file.txt
```

Test compressed file integrity:
```
pigz -t file.txt.gz
```

## Environment Variables

- **GZIP**: Options read from this variable before command line options
- **PIGZ**: Options read from this variable after GZIP but before command line options

## File Formats

pigz produces standard gzip, zlib, or zip format output. Any tool that can decompress these formats can decompress pigz output, and pigz can decompress any standard gzip file.

## Performance

The input is broken into chunks that are compressed in parallel. Each chunk is compressed independently with the last 32K of the previous chunk used as a dictionary to maintain compression effectiveness. The number of threads defaults to the number of available processors.

Decompression uses a single thread for the actual decompression, but creates additional threads for reading, writing, and checksum calculation.

## More Information

For complete documentation, see the pigz man page (pigz.1 or pigz.pdf).

## Author

pigz was written by Mark Adler.

.TH PIGZ 1 "August 19, 2023"
.SH NAME
pigz, unpigz \- compress or expand files
.SH SYNOPSIS
.ll +8
.B pigz
.RB [ " \-cdfhikKlLmMnNqrRtz0..9,11 " ]
[
.B -b
.I blocksize
]
[
.B -p
.I threads
]
[
.B -S
.I suffix
]
[
.I "name \&..."
]
.ll -8
.br
.B unpigz
.RB [ " \-cfhikKlLmMnNqrRtz " ]
[
.B -b
.I blocksize
]
[
.B -p
.I threads
]
[
.B -S
.I suffix
]
[
.I "name \&..."
]
.SH DESCRIPTION
.I Pigz
compresses using threads to make use of multiple processors and cores.
The input is broken up into 128 KB chunks with each compressed in parallel.
The individual check value for each chunk is also calculated in parallel.
The compressed data is written in order to the output, and a combined check
value is calculated from the individual check values.
.PP
The compressed data format generated is in the gzip, zlib, or single-entry
zip format using the deflate compression method.  The compression produces
partial raw deflate streams which are concatenated by a single write thread
and wrapped with the appropriate header and trailer, where the trailer
contains the combined check value.
.PP
Each partial raw deflate stream is terminated by an empty stored block
(using the Z_SYNC_FLUSH option of zlib), in order to end that partial bit
stream at a byte boundary.  That allows the partial streams to be
concatenated simply as sequences of bytes.  This adds a very small four to
five byte overhead to the output for each input chunk.
.PP
The default input block size is 128K, but can be changed with the
.B -b
option.  The number of compress threads is set by default to the number
of online processors,
which can be changed using the
.B -p
option.  Specifying
.B -p 1
avoids the use of threads entirely.
.PP
The input blocks, while compressed independently, have the last 32K of the
previous block loaded as a preset dictionary to preserve the compression
effectiveness of deflating in a single thread.  This can be turned off using
the
.B -i
or
.B --independent
option, so that the blocks can be decompressed
independently for partial error recovery or for random access. This also
inserts an extra empty block to flag independent blocks by prefacing
each with the nine-byte sequence (in hex): 00 00 FF FF 00 00 00 FF FF.
.PP
Decompression can't be parallelized, at least not without specially prepared
deflate streams for that purpose.  As a result,
.I pigz
uses a single thread
(the main thread) for decompression, but will create three other threads for
reading, writing, and check calculation, which can speed up decompression
under some circumstances.  Parallel decompression can be turned off by
specifying one process
(
.B -dp 1
or
.B -tp 1
).
.PP
All options on the command line are processed before any names are processed.
If no names are provided on the command line, or if "-" is given as a name (but
not after "--"), then the input is taken from stdin. If the GZIP or PIGZ
environment variables are set, then options are taken from their values before
any command line options are processed, first from GZIP, then from PIGZ.
.PP
Compressed files can be restored to their original form using
.I pigz -d
or
.I unpigz.

.SH OPTIONS
.TP
.B -# --fast --best
Regulate the speed of compression using the specified digit
.IR # ,
where
.B \-1
or
.B \-\-fast
indicates the fastest compression method (less compression)
and
.B \-9
or
.B \-\-best
indicates the slowest compression method (best compression).
.B -0
is no compression.
.B \-11
gives a few percent better compression at a severe cost in execution time,
using the zopfli algorithm by Jyrki Alakuijala.
The default is
.B \-6.
.TP
.B -A --alias xxx
Use xxx as the name for any --zip entry from stdin (the default name is "-").
.TP
.B -b --blocksize mmm
Set compression block size to mmmK (default 128KiB).
.TP
.B -c --stdout --to-stdout
Write all processed output to stdout (won't delete).
.TP
.B -C --comment ccc
Include the provided comment in the gzip header or zip central file header.
.TP
.B -d --decompress --uncompress
Decompress the compressed input.
.TP
.B -f --force
Force overwrite, compress .gz, links, and to terminal.
.TP
.B -h --help
Display a help screen and quit.
.TP
.B -H --huffman
Compress using the Huffman-only strategy.
.TP
.B -i --independent
Compress blocks independently for damage recovery.
.TP
.B -k --keep
Do not delete original file after processing.
.TP
.B -K --zip
Compress to PKWare zip (.zip) single entry format.
.TP
.B -l --list
List the contents of the compressed input.
.TP
.B -L --license
Display the
.I pigz
license and quit.
.TP
.B -m --no-time
Do not store or restore the modification time. -Nm will store or restore the
name, but not the modification time. Note that the order of the options is
important.
.TP
.B -M --time
Store or restore the modification time. -nM will store or restore the

        # parse gzip header: ID1 ID2 CM FLG MTIME XFL OS
        flg=data[3]
        mtime=struct.unpack("<I", data[4:8])[0]
        print(f"  FLG={flg:02x} MTIME={mtime} XFL={data[8]:02x} OS={data[9]:02x}")
        # if FNAME present, extract?
        # FLG bits: FTEXT 1, FHCRC 2, FEXTRA 4, FNAME 8, FCOMMENT 16
        pos=10
        if flg & 4:
            xlen=struct.unpack("<H", data[pos:pos+2])[0]
            print(f"  EXTRA len={xlen} bytes={data[pos+2:pos+2+xlen].hex()[:100]}")
            pos+=2+xlen
        if flg & 8:
            end=data.index(b"\x00",pos)
            print(f"  FNAME={data[pos:end]!r}")
            pos=end+1
        if flg & 16:
            end=data.index(b"\x00",pos)
            print(f"  FCOMMENT={data[pos:end]!r}")
            pos=end+1
        if flg & 2:
            print(f"  FHCRC present")
        # try decompress
        try:
            dec=gzip.decompress(data)
            print(f"  decompress ok len {len(dec)} match {dec[:20]!r}")
        except Exception as e:
            print("  decompress fail",e)

.TH PIGZ 1 "August 19, 2023"
.SH NAME
pigz, unpigz \- compress or expand files
.SH SYNOPSIS
.ll +8
.B pigz
.RB [ " \-cdfhikKlLmMnNqrRtz0..9,11 " ]
[
.B -b
.I blocksize
]
[
.B -p
.I threads
]
[
.B -S
.I suffix
]
[
.I "name \&..."
]
.ll -8
.br
.B unpigz
.RB [ " \-cfhikKlLmMnNqrRtz " ]
[
.B -b
.I blocksize
]
[
.B -p
.I threads
]
[
.B -S
.I suffix
]
[
.I "name \&..."
]
.SH DESCRIPTION
.I Pigz
compresses using threads to make use of multiple processors and cores.
The input is broken up into 128 KB chunks with each compressed in parallel.
The individual check value for each chunk is also calculated in parallel.
The compressed data is written in order to the output, and a combined check
value is calculated from the individual check values.
.PP
The compressed data format generated is in the gzip, zlib, or single-entry
zip format using the deflate compression method.  The compression produces
partial raw deflate streams which are concatenated by a single write thread
and wrapped with the appropriate header and trailer, where the trailer
contains the combined check value.
.PP
Each partial raw deflate stream is terminated by an empty stored block
(using the Z_SYNC_FLUSH option of zlib), in order to end that partial bit
stream at a byte boundary.  That allows the partial streams to be
concatenated simply as sequences of bytes.  This adds a very small four to
five byte overhead to the output for each input chunk.
.PP
The default input block size is 128K, but can be changed with the
.B -b
option.  The number of compress threads is set by default to the number
of online processors,
which can be changed using the
.B -p
option.  Specifying
.B -p 1
avoids the use of threads entirely.
.PP
The input blocks, while compressed independently, have the last 32K of the
previous block loaded as a preset dictionary to preserve the compression
effectiveness of deflating in a single thread.  This can be turned off using
the
.B -i
or
.B --independent
option, so that the blocks can be decompressed
independently for partial error recovery or for random access. This also
inserts an extra empty block to flag independent blocks by prefacing
each with the nine-byte sequence (in hex): 00 00 FF FF 00 00 00 FF FF.
.PP
Decompression can't be parallelized, at least not without specially prepared
deflate streams for that purpose.  As a result,
.I pigz
uses a single thread
(the main thread) for decompression, but will create three other threads for
reading, writing, and check calculation, which can speed up decompression
under some circumstances.  Parallel decompression can be turned off by
specifying one process
(
.B -dp 1
or
.B -tp 1
).
.PP
All options on the command line are processed before any names are processed.
If no names are provided on the command line, or if "-" is given as a name (but
not after "--"), then the input is taken from stdin. If the GZIP or PIGZ
environment variables are set, then options are taken from their values before
any command line options are processed, first from GZIP, then from PIGZ.
.PP
Compressed files can be restored to their original form using
.I pigz -d
or
.I unpigz.

.SH OPTIONS
.TP
.B -# --fast --best
Regulate the speed of compression using the specified digit
.IR # ,
where
.B \-1
or
.B \-\-fast
indicates the fastest compression method (less compression)
and
.B \-9
or
.B \-\-best
indicates the slowest compression method (best compression).
.B -0
is no compression.
.B \-11
gives a few percent better compression at a severe cost in execution time,
using the zopfli algorithm by Jyrki Alakuijala.
The default is
.B \-6.
.TP
.B -A --alias xxx
Use xxx as the name for any --zip entry from stdin (the default name is "-").
.TP
.B -b --blocksize mmm
Set compression block size to mmmK (default 128KiB).
.TP
.B -c --stdout --to-stdout
Write all processed output to stdout (won't delete).
.TP
.B -C --comment ccc
Include the provided comment in the gzip header or zip central file header.
.TP
.B -d --decompress --uncompress
Decompress the compressed input.
.TP
.B -f --force
Force overwrite, compress .gz, links, and to terminal.
.TP
.B -h --help
Display a help screen and quit.
.TP
.B -H --huffman
Compress using the Huffman-only strategy.
.TP
.B -i --independent
Compress blocks independently for damage recovery.
.TP
.B -k --keep
Do not delete original file after processing.
.TP
.B -K --zip
Compress to PKWare zip (.zip) single entry format.
.TP
.B -l --list
List the contents of the compressed input.
.TP
.B -L --license
Display the
.I pigz
license and quit.
.TP
.B -m --no-time
Do not store or restore the modification time. -Nm will store or restore the
name, but not the modification time. Note that the order of the options is
important.
.TP
.B -M --time
Store or restore the modification time. -nM will store or restore the
modification time, but not the name. Note that the order of the options is
important. Modification times are stored only for regular files, not pipes.
.TP
.B -n --no-name
Do not store or restore the file name or the modification time. This is the
default when decompressing. When the file name is not restored from the header,
the name of the compressed file with the suffix stripped is the name of the
decompressed file. When the modification time is not restored from the header,
the modification time of the compressed file is used (not the current time).
.TP
.B -N --name
Store or restore both the file name and the modification time. This is the
default when compressing.
.TP
.B -p --processes n
Allow up to n processes (default is the number of online processors)
.TP
.B -q --quiet --silent
Print no messages, even on error.
.TP
.B -r --recursive
Process the contents of all subdirectories.
.TP
.B -R --rsyncable
Input-determined block locations for rsync.
.TP
.B -S --suffix .sss
Use suffix .sss instead of .gz (for compression).
.TP
.B -t --test
Test the integrity of the compressed input.
.TP
.B -U --rle
Compress using the run length encoding strategy.
.TP
.B -v --verbose
Provide more verbose output.

EXE="/workspace/executable"
def run(args, input_data=None, env=None, cwd="/tmp"):
    import subprocess as sp
    e=dict(os.environ)
    if env is not None:
        e.update(env)
    r=sp.run(args, input=input_data, capture_output=True, env=e, cwd=cwd)
    return r

# From behavior: -T behaves like -m (no-time) but with order sensitivity same as -m?
# Check TN vs Nm:
# -Nm => store name not time, -TN => store both (i.e., T before N means N wins). So T == m exactly.
# -MT vs -mM? Actually -mM => time stored? Let's test mM, MT etc.
import tempfile, struct, os
tmpdir=tempfile.mkdtemp()
fpath=os.path.join(tmpdir,"hello.txt")
open(fpath,"wb").write(b"hello world\n"*1000)
os.utime(fpath,(1234567890,1234567890))
def hdr(opts):
    r=run([EXE,"-c"]+opts+[fpath], cwd=tmpdir)
    data=r.stdout
    flg=data[3]
    mtime=struct.unpack("<I", data[4:8])[0]
    return flg, mtime
for opts in [["-m","-M"],["-M","-m"],["-T","-M"],["-M","-T"],["-T","-m"],["-m","-T"],["-n","-T"],["-T","-n"],["-N","-T"],["-T","-N"]]:
    flg,mtime=hdr(opts)
    print(opts, f"FLG={flg:02x} MTIME={mtime}")

# Also Check what pigz.1 says about -T? Synopsis includes T? Let's view remainder
txt=open("pigz.1").read()
print(txt[6000:12000])

PY

def run(args, input_data=None, env=None, cwd="/tmp"):

            os.remove(os.path.join(tmpdir,"a.txt"))

import subprocess, os, tempfile
EXE="/workspace/executable"
def run(args, input_data=None, env=None, cwd="/tmp"):
    import subprocess as sp
    e=dict(os.environ)
    if env is not None:
        e.update(env)
    r=sp.run(args, input=input_data, capture_output=True, env=e, cwd=cwd)
    return r
tmpdir=tempfile.mkdtemp()
print(tmpdir)
def mk(name, content=b"hello world "*100):
    p=os.path.join(tmpdir,name)
    open(p,"wb").write(content)
    return p
# compress suffix tests
for opts in [[],["-z"],["-K"],["-S",".foo"],["-z","-S",".foo"],["-K","-S",".foo"],["-S",".foo","-z"],["-S",".foo","-K"]]:
    fname=mk("suf_test.txt")
    r=run([EXE,"-k"]+opts+[fname], cwd=tmpdir)
    print(f"opts={opts} rc={r.returncode} err={r.stderr[:100]!r} files={[x for x in os.listdir(tmpdir) if x.startswith('suf_test')]}")
    # cleanup gz files
    for f in list(os.listdir(tmpdir)):
        if f.startswith("suf_test") and f!="suf_test.txt":
            os.remove(os.path.join(tmpdir,f))
    os.remove(fname) if os.path.exists(fname) else None

# compress file that already has suffix? e.g., file.gz compress?
f=mk("already.gz", b"hello")
r=run([EXE,"-k",f], cwd=tmpdir)
print(f"compress .gz file rc={r.returncode} err={r.stderr}")
# with -f?
r=run([EXE,"-k","-f",f], cwd=tmpdir)
print(f"compress .gz -f rc={r.returncode} err={r.stderr} files={os.listdir(tmpdir)}")
# cleanup
for f in list(os.listdir(tmpdir)):
    try: os.remove(os.path.join(tmpdir,f))
    except: pass

# Test file with no suffix decompress?
f=mk("nosuf", b"hello")
# write gzdata to nosuf?
gzdata=run([EXE,"-c",os.path.join(tmpdir,"base.txt") if os.path.exists(os.path.join(tmpdir,"base.txt")) else mk("base.txt")], cwd=tmpdir).stdout
open(os.path.join(tmpdir,"nosuf2"),"wb").write(gzdata)
r=run([EXE,"-d",os.path.join(tmpdir,"nosuf2")], cwd=tmpdir)
print("nosuf decompress",r.returncode, r.stderr)

# Test short names: file named ".gz", "a", "a.", etc
for name in [".gz","a","a.",".z","-gz"]:
    p=os.path.join(tmpdir,name)
    try: open(p,"wb").write(gzdata)
    except Exception as e: print(e); continue
    r=run([EXE,"-d",p], cwd=tmpdir)
    print(f"name={name!r} rc={r.returncode} err={r.stderr!r} dir={os.listdir(tmpdir)}")
    for f in list(os.listdir(tmpdir)):
        if f not in ["base.txt"]:
            try: os.remove(os.path.join(tmpdir,f))
            except: pass
    open(os.path.join(tmpdir,"base.txt"),"wb").write(b"hello world "*100)

# pigz - Parallel Implementation of GZip

pigz (pronounced "pig-zee") is a parallel implementation of gzip that compresses files using multiple processors and cores.

## What pigz does

pigz is a fully functional replacement for gzip that exploits multiple processors and multiple cores to compress data faster. It can compress and decompress files in gzip, zlib, and zip formats.

## Basic Usage

```
pigz [options] [files...]
unpigz [options] [files...]
```

If no files are specified or "-" is given as a filename, pigz reads from standard input.

## Key Features

- **Parallel compression**: Splits input into chunks (default 128 KB) and compresses them in parallel
